# The other AI

## A map

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Kraemer et al. 2025 pair eight tasks with the AI methods used for
  them
- The hosts' reinforcement learning sits on two rows
- Building and checking the model itself is not a row
:::

## Learn the part of the mechanism you do not know

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A universal differential equation keeps the compartments and
  replaces one term with a neural network
- On epidemic data the network soaks up identifiability. The fitted
  mechanistic parameters "did not match the published values"
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-ude.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="An SEIR box diagram, S to E to I to R, with the transmission
rate beta of t replaced by a small red neural network glyph feeding the
S to E flow."}

::: {.attribution}
Rackauckas et al. 2020, [arXiv:2001.04385](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04385)
· Philipps, Schmid and Hasenauer 2025, npj Systems Biology and
Applications, [PMC12398592](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12398592/)
· Millevoi, Pasetto and Ferronato 2024, PLoS Comput Biol, on

## Fit models you could not fit

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Simulate many parameter and data pairs, then train a network to map
  data to a posterior. No likelihood needed
- OutbreakFlow did this for early COVID-19 in Germany. Pinotti et al.
  fitted an SEIR model to the 2014 Sierra Leone Ebola data with neural
  posterior estimation
- Non-identifiability comes from the simulator. "Additional simulations
  alone cannot resolve" it
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-sbi.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A simulator box feeds many simulated parameter and data pairs
into a network that learns the posterior, a normalising flow. Observed
data enter the trained network and a red posterior density comes out,
labelled posterior in seconds."}

::: {.attribution}
Radev et al. 2021, *OutbreakFlow*, PLoS Comput Biol,
[doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009472](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009472)
· Pinotti et al. 2025, bioRxiv,
[doi:10.1101/2025.11.25.690436](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.11.25.690436v1)
· Jang, Candan and Chowell 2026, PLoS Comput Biol,
[PMC13252848](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13252848/)

## Forecast without a mechanism

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Pretrained on many series from other domains. Your series in, a
  forecast out, no fitting
- Strong short-term accuracy on sparse or irregular data. TabPFN-TS,
  zero-shot, rivalled the ECDC RespiCast ensemble on influenza-like
  illness in nine countries
- Less is reported about peaks and turning points
- "Predictive models either need a lot of data or very good theory"
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-foundation.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A stack of many grey time series labelled many series, many
domains, feeds a slate box labelled one pretrained model, a transformer,
which produces a red forecast fan on a teal epidemic curve to the right,
labelled your series in, a forecast out, no mechanism anywhere."}

::: {.attribution}
Kalahasti et al. 2025, medRxiv,
